speaker: Doctor
text: That sensation of air getting stuck on exhalation is a classic sign of airway obstruction. Given your normal FeNO and eosinophil counts, this points away from typical allergic asthma. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction (EIB) with mild persistent airway hyperresponsiveness. The significant improvement in FEV1 after bronchodilator use, combined with your history of exertional dyspnea and normal inflammatory markers, confirms reversible airway obstruction likely triggered by physical activity. I recommend a trial of a short-acting beta-agonist before exercise and an inhaled corticosteroid to prevent future episodes.
